$$\forall b\in\mathbb{N},\ b>0\ \ \exists N,k\in\mathbb{N}:\quad \Bigl(b\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\omega(N+1+j)\,2^{\,k-1-j}\Bigr)\bmod 2^{k} \;+\; b\bigl(\log_{2}(N+k+1)+1\bigr) < 2^{k}$$

Under the hypotheses that the Lambert identity ∑_{n≥0} ω(n)/2^n = ∑_p 1/(2^p − 1) holds, that every rescaled tail splits as T(N) = ∑_{j<k} ω(N+1+j)/2^{j+1} + T(N+k)/2^k, that every T(M) is positive, and that T(M) ≤ log₂(M+1) + 1 for every M, for every positive natural b there are naturals N and k such that the residue mod 2^k of the integer b·∑_{j<k} ω(N+1+j)·2^{k−1−j}, plus b(log₂(N+k+1) + 1), is less than 2^k. The sum, the product and the residue are computed in ℕ (with k − 1 − j truncated subtraction, which is 0 when k = 0) and then cast to ℝ, where log₂ is `Real.logb 2`; here T(M) denotes the rescaled tail ∑_{j≥0} ω(M+1+j)/2^{j+1}, a tsum over ℝ (0 if not summable), and ω(n) is the number of distinct prime factors of n.
label: Crux window whose residue leaves room below 2^k
